Shri Nitin Dubey - Advocate for the applicant.
Ms. Mamta Mishra - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/St  ORDER

This is repeat (fifth) bail application filed on behalf of applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
2.

The applicant is in jail since 19.05.2023 in connection with Crime No. 88 of 2023 registered at P.S. Patan, District-Jabalpur for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366-A and 376 of the IPC and under Section 5/6 of POCSO Act, 2012.

3. Applicant's first application was dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 17.08.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.32482 of 2023, second application was dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 22.11.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.42364 of 2023, third application was dismissed as withdrawn by order 16.04.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.No.6258 of 2024 and fourth application was also dismissed as withdrawn by order 30.01.2025 passed in M.Cr.C.No.55449 of 2024.

Prosecution story in brief is that applicant repeatedly committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on minor prosecutrix.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that in the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., no allegation of penetrative sexual assault has been made.
It is also urged that as per statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix had left her house at her own along with applicant.
It is also urged that statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., it is stated that the parties have solemnized the marriage and they were living as husband and wife.
Further, learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is in jail since 19.05.2023 and the trial is still pending.
On above grounds, it is urged that applicant be released on bail.
6. Learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has opposed the application.
7. Looking to overall facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.

8. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
9. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.

However, in NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:36881 3 MCRC-22747-2025 case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
10. Soft copy of this bail order be sent immediately/forthwith to the applicant through concerned Jail Superintendent.
11. M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
12. Certified copy as per rules.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE vai Brijesh Kumar Silawat Ladiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157305003/
